budget_items.what_was_said: The outgoing chair said that despite the override passing, several teaching and support positions are being eliminated because the cuts equal expiring ESSER funds; paraprofessional positions are not part of this round of cuts.

A select board member described a proposed multi-year task force to review town and school revenue, costs and borrowing capacity; the school committee deferred deciding whether to name a representative.
The board authorized spending caps on student activity accounts for the coming year, set per school.

A member noted the town spent a large amount on the retired curriculum materials now being declared surplus and asked whether some titles could be resold or kept for the library rather than discarded.
The board accepted four scholarships from a donor for graduating students pursuing creative writing and film production.
The board accepted a PTO check from the spring book fair, to be deposited into the Student Activities account to support future primary school field trips.

decisions.decision: Vote on minutes in two batches, taking the May 14 special meeting separately since one member was absent that day
Table naming a school committee representative to the proposed budget task force and revisit it at a future meeting
Defer any sale or transfer of surplus curriculum materials until the librarian can review them in late August
Members will send potential FY superintendent goals to Dr. Burnham over the summer ahead of a fall vote

minutes.headline: School Committee confirms staff cuts proceed despite the override, tied to expiring ESSER funds
minutes.summary: This was the school committee's annual reorganization meeting: a new chair and vice chair were elected, subcommittee and liaison assignments were made, and routine annual authorizations (policies, student activity accounts, the town-meeting auditorium waiver) were approved. The chair's report disclosed that several teaching and support positions are being cut despite the override passing, because the cuts equal expiring ESSER funds; the board also declared old curriculum materials surplus, accepted donations, approved the superintendent's two-year evaluation, and tabled naming a representative to a proposed town budget task force.

what_happened.line: The outgoing chair reported that several teaching and support positions are being cut even though the override passed, because the cuts match expiring ESSER funds.
The committee completed its annual reorganization, electing a new chair and vice chair.
A proposal for a multi-year town budget task force to review town and school finances was raised, and the committee tabled naming its own representative to it.
The committee declared retired curriculum materials surplus, deferring any sale until the librarian reviews them in August.

why_it_matters: Positions funded by federal COVID relief are ending on schedule regardless of the override outcome, so some staffing reductions are happening in the same year residents approved new school funding.
A seat on a proposed town-wide budget task force remains unfilled, which affects who represents school interests in any joint review of town and school revenue and borrowing capacity.
Paraprofessional positions were explicitly excluded from this round of cuts, which matters to families relying on that support in classrooms.
watch_next: A future school committee meeting where a representative to the town budget task force may be named
A fall vote on the superintendent's goals, based on suggestions members send over the summer

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree closely on every vote that both captured — chair/vice-chair elections, policy reauthorization, student activity accounts, surplus materials (with Brzozoski's abstention), donations, and the superintendent evaluation all match once the caption-mangled names (Leighton→Lehtinen, Scuollo-Brini→Sculimbrene, Areno→Archambault, Brzozowski→Brzozoski) are resolved. The main things a reader should check: three votes our captions marked "not audible" that the official minutes record as passed (secretary election, appointments slate, auditorium waiver), a scholarship total that may be 4x ours ($1,000 vs. official's "4 scholarships...$1,000 each"), and three decisions in our minutes — the budget task force tabling, deferring the surplus-materials sale, and the summer superintendent-goals process — that do not appear in the official minutes at all.
